# KIT-OWNED: do not edit locally; change it in the kit and re-sync.
# What a Claude Code pane looks like when it waits for a person. Kit-owned: read by
# scripts/watch_workers.sh, and through it by scripts/spawn_worker.sh, so the folder-trust
# dialog and every other wait are defined once, here.
#
# One rule per line: KIND STATUS VERSION WHERE ERE (the ERE is the rest of the line).
#   KIND     what waits; a session is WAITING on KIND when one `last` rule of KIND matches the
#            last non-empty line of the pane AND one `near` rule of KIND matches one of the
#            last 15 non-empty lines.
#   STATUS   VERIFIED: written from a real pane captured on VERSION (the capture is a test
#            fixture under tests/fixtures/panes/ in the kit). UNVERIFIED: a guess nobody has
#            seen on a real pane; it ships because a missed wait costs more than a false one.
#   WHERE    last | near (above), or status: the context rule below, which never makes a
#            session WAITING.
#   ERE      grep -E, matched byte by byte (LC_ALL=C) on the line with control bytes removed
#            and trailing blanks stripped.
#
# Why the bottom of the pane and not a phrase anywhere: a worker's OUTPUT can quote "Do you
# want to proceed?" (a diff of a document about prompts). While the TUI works, its last lines
# are the input box and the mode line; only a dialog puts its own key hint on the last line.
# A rule never matches on a phrase alone, and the key hint is required on the LAST line.
#
# A new Claude Code version can change any of this. When a session blocked and the watcher
# said nothing, capture its pane (`tmux capture-pane -p -J -t =NAME:`), add it as a fixture,
# and add or correct the rule here with that version.

# The folder-trust dialog (also what spawn_worker.sh stops on).
trust       VERIFIED    2.1.285  last  ^ *Enter to confirm · Esc to cancel$
trust       VERIFIED    2.1.285  near  ^ *(❯ )?(No, exit|Yes, I trust this folder)$
# An older wording of the same dialog, from the text spawn_worker.sh matched before.
trust       UNVERIFIED  -        last  Esc to (cancel|exit)$
trust       UNVERIFIED  -        near  Do you trust the files in this folder

# A tool permission prompt ("Do you want to proceed?" over numbered Yes/No options).
permission  VERIFIED    2.1.285  last  ^ *Esc to cancel · Tab to amend$
permission  VERIFIED    2.1.285  near  ^ *(❯ )?[0-9]+\. (Yes|No)
# A question the model asks with its question tool (numbered options, free-text option).
question    VERIFIED    2.1.285  last  ^ *Enter to select · ↑/↓ to navigate · Esc to cancel$
question    VERIFIED    2.1.285  near  ^ *(❯ )?[0-9]+\. [^ ]
# Any other numbered choice that ends in a cancel hint (an edit prompt, a plan approval).
dialog      UNVERIFIED  -        last  Esc to cancel
dialog      UNVERIFIED  -        near  ^ *❯ [0-9]+\. [^ ]

# The context figure in the status line, <used>/<window> with a k or M on each ("Opus 5.5
# 58k/1.0M high", between `│` separators). The watcher reports it past --context-warn; a
# status line without it is reported once as unparsable, never guessed. Unlike the rules
# above, its ERE is matched by awk against each blank-separated word of the pane's lines.
context     VERIFIED    2.1.285  status  ^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?[kM]/[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?[kM]$
